title: Adaptive warmup routing and attention pulse aligner for continuous batching
creator: Rafael Gomez
description: Sustained microbursts and mixed sequence-length traffic are causing 95th+ tail spikes on the hosted API. Current admission logic routes requests by quota windows and simple length heuristics which often forces long sequences into slow tiled kernels during warmup, increasing prefill latency and exacerbating decode tail. This ticket experiments with an adaptive warmup routing layer and an 'attention pulse aligner' that coordinates short/long request admission and kernel selection to reduce tail latency while preserving throughput.
proposal: Introduce a lightweight warmup routing stage before the admission queue that: 1) classifies incoming requests into transient-short, steady-long, and streaming categories using recent per-client sequence histograms; 2) assigns a warmup profile that fast-paths likely short-prefill requests to fused attention kernels with temporary KV-reservation heuristics; 3) staggers long-prefill admission (small deferred slots) while keeping decode-ready short requests moving to maintain GPU utilization and reduce head-of-line blocking. The attention pulse aligner will emit soft alignment hints to the kernel selector for coalescing attention execution windows across slots to minimize kernel launch overheads.
design_decisions: Keep warmup router stateless at per-worker level with only small ring buffers for sequence histograms to avoid cross-worker contention
Use probabilistic short-path eligibility (not absolute) to preserve fairness under adversarial workloads
Emit kernel hints as part of admission metadata rather than changing kernel selector API; kernel selector will optionally honor hints based on free compute budget
Do not increase persistent KV-reservation until canary shows <3% throughput regression
Fallback to existing admission logic if warmup routing is disabled or if kernel hints conflict with runtime constraints
implementation_notes: Add WarmupRouter module in serving/runtime/admission with unit tests for histogram decay and classification thresholds
Extend admission envelope to include 'kernel_hint' and 'warmup_profile' string fields
Update kernel selector to accept hint precedence level; low-cost fused kernels should be prioritized for 'short' hints
Instrument a new tracing span 'warmup.router' and add metrics: warmup_class_pct_by_client, kernel_hint_honor_rate, warmup_queue_hold_ms
Create a canary rollout for 5% of traffic routed by region with runtime flag 'warmup_v1'
test_plan: Unit tests for histogram decayer and classification thresholds
Integration tests simulating mixed traffic (80% short, 20% long) and verifying short-path admission rates
Perf microbench with CPU/GPU containers: measure p50/p95/p99 prefill and decode latencies under 10k RPS mixed workload
Canary in prod: enable for 5% traffic, collect metrics for 48 hours and compare to baseline dashboard
A/B evaluation comparing kernel hint honor enabled vs disabled to detect any throughput regressions
perf_targets: Reduce p95 prefill latency by >= 20% on mixed traffic traces compared to baseline
Keep median token decode latency within +5% of baseline
No more than 1% throughput degradation on canary traffic
Kernel hint honor rate >= 75% under normal load
